intro_en: In this lesson you will learn to tell the time and say the days of the week. You will also talk about your day: "I get up at seven in the morning", "I work from nine to five". Verbs (action words) come in for the first time. 〜ます = I do. 〜ません = I don’t do. 〜ました = I did. 〜ませんでした = I didn’t do. As in Tamil, the verb comes at the end of the sentence. Time (past or not) and "not" are added as endings on the verb itself.

g04-1.explanation_en: To tell the time, use number + 時 (じ, o’clock / மணி) + number + 分 (ふん/ぷん, minutes / நிமிடம்). "What time is it now?" = 「今 何時ですか」. The answer is 「今 九時十分です」. For half past, use 半 (はん). 七時半 = half past seven (ஏழரை மணி). Tamil says "ஏழரை" (seven and a half). In the same way, "half" comes after the number. To show morning or afternoon, put 午前 (a.m.) or 午後 (p.m.) before the time: 午後 三時. This is the same order as Tamil "மதியம் மூன்று மணி" (afternoon three o’clock). Learn these sound changes by heart. 四時 = よじ, 七時 = しちじ, 九時 = くじ. 一分 = いっぷん, 三分 = さんぷん, 四分 = よんぷん, 六分 = ろっぷん, 八分 = はっぷん, 十分 = じゅっぷん, 何分 = なんぷん. The others use ふん: 二分 にふん, 五分 ごふん.
g04-1.tamil_parallel_en: இப்போது மணி ஏழரை "It is half past seven now" = 今 七時半です。 Here 時 is roughly "மணி" (o’clock). 分 is "நிமிடம்" (minute). 半 is "அரை" (half). It comes after the number, just like Tamil "ஏழரை".
g04-1.formation_en: 今 + (午前 / 午後) + number 時 + number 分 / 半 + です ; 今 何時ですか
g04-1.pitfalls_en: 四時 = よじ (not よんじ). 九時 = くじ (not きゅうじ). 半 must go after 時: 七時半. 半七時 is wrong. Don’t put 午後 after the time. 三時午後 is wrong.

g04-2.explanation_en: The polite form of a Japanese verb (action word) ends in 〜ます. 起きます = I get up. 寝ます = I sleep / go to bed. 働きます = I work. It is used for things you do every day ("I get up every day"). It is also used for the future ("I will work tomorrow"). Tamil has different forms for now and for the future. Japanese uses the same form for both. Words like 毎日 (every day) and 明日 (tomorrow) tell you the meaning. To say "not", change ます → ません. 働きません = "I don’t work / I won’t work". To ask a question, add か as usual: 働きますか. As in Tamil, the verb comes at the end of the sentence. You can often drop "I".
g04-2.tamil_parallel_en: நாளை வேலை செய்வேன் "I will work tomorrow" / புதன்கிழமை வேலை செய்வதில்லை "I don’t work on Wednesdays" = 明日 働きます。/ 水曜日は 働きません。 Tamil uses different forms for the future and for habits. Japanese uses one ます form for both.
g04-2.formation_en: V (ます-form): 起きます → 起きません ; 寝ます → 寝ません ; 働きます → 働きません
g04-2.pitfalls_en: The 〜ます form does not change for "I", "you" or "he". Tamil changes the ending, as in "செய்கிறேன்" (I do) / "செய்கிறார்" (he does). Japanese does not. 働きます is the same for everyone. Don’t mix up ません with じゃありません. じゃありません is for nouns.

g04-3.explanation_en: For the past, change ます → ました. 起きました = I got up. 寝ました = I slept. 働きました = I worked. For "did not", use ません + でした = ませんでした. 働きませんでした = I didn’t work. Tamil puts the time inside the verb, as in "செய்-த்-ஏன்" (I did). In the same way, in Japanese the time shows only in the verb ending. With time words like "yesterday" and "last night", you must use the past form.
g04-3.tamil_parallel_en: நேற்று வேலை செய்தேன் "I worked yesterday" / நேற்று வேலை செய்யவில்லை "I didn’t work yesterday" = 昨日 働きました。/ 昨日 働きませんでした。 Like Tamil, the verb ending shows both the past and "not".
g04-3.formation_en: V ます → V ました ; V ません → V ませんでした
g04-3.pitfalls_en: Don’t use the past twice, as in 「働きましたでした」. That is wrong. ませんでした is one block. Don’t write ませんした.

g04-4.explanation_en: To say the exact time something happens, put に after the time. 「六時に 起きます」 = "I get up at six o’clock" (ஆறு மணிக்கு எழுந்திருக்கிறேன்). に is the "-க்கு" (at) in the Tamil "ஆறு மணி-க்கு". You can also put に after days of the week. 「日曜日に」 = on Sunday (ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமையன்று). But don’t put に after words like 今日, 明日, 昨日, 毎日, 毎朝, 毎晩, 今, 朝 and 晩. These words have no number. They depend on when you are speaking. Be careful here. Spoken Tamil often says "நாளைக்கு" (tomorrow, with "-க்கு"). But Japanese never says 明日に. Just say 明日 働きます. Time with a number → に. Word with no number, like "tomorrow" → no に.
g04-4.tamil_parallel_en: ஆறு மணிக்கு எழுந்திருக்கிறேன் "I get up at six o’clock" = 六時に 起きます。 Here に is roughly the Tamil "-க்கு" (at) after a time.
g04-4.formation_en: Time (number / day of the week) + に + V ; 今日・明日・毎日 + V (no に)
g04-4.pitfalls_en: 「明日に」「毎日に」「今に」 are wrong. In 「毎朝 七時に」, 毎朝 takes no に. Only 七時 takes に, because it has a number.

g04-5.explanation_en: から = "from" (-இலிருந்து / முதல்). まで = "until / to" (வரை). 「九時から 五時まで 働きます」 = "I work from nine o’clock to five o’clock" (ஒன்பது மணி முதல் ஐந்து மணி வரை வேலை செய்கிறேன்). Like the Tamil "-இலிருந்து" and "-வரை", they go after the noun. The order is the same as Tamil. You can use them together or alone. For shop or bank hours, you can end with just です. 「銀行は 九時から 三時までです」. Tamil says the same: "வங்கி ஒன்பது முதல் மூன்று வரை" (the bank is from nine to three).
g04-5.tamil_parallel_en: ஒன்பது மணி முதல் ஐந்து மணி வரை வேலை செய்கிறேன் "I work from nine to five" = 九時から 五時まで 働きます。 Here から is roughly "-இலிருந்து" (from). まで is "-வரை" (until). The order is the same as Tamil.
g04-5.formation_en: N1 + から + N2 + まで + V / です
g04-5.pitfalls_en: Don’t add に after から or まで. 「九時からに」 is wrong. まで only means "until". "By" a deadline is a different form. You will learn it in a later lesson.

g04-6.explanation_en: To join two nouns with "and", use と. 「土曜日と 日曜日」 = Saturday and Sunday (சனிக்கிழமையும் ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமையும்). In Tamil we add "-உம்" to both, as in "சனி-யும் ஞாயிறு-ம்". In Japanese, と comes only after the first noun. と only joins nouns. It does not join two sentences or two verbs. Don’t mix it up with も (too / also). と = "and" in a list. も = "this one too".
g04-6.tamil_parallel_en: சனிக்கிழமையும் ஞாயிற்றுக்கிழமையும் "Saturday and Sunday" = 土曜日と 日曜日. Tamil puts "-உம்" on both nouns. Japanese と goes only after the first one.
g04-6.pitfalls_en: Tamil speakers may want to add と at the end too, as in 「土曜日と 日曜日と」. Don’t do this. You can’t join verbs with と, as in "I get up and work".

g04-7.explanation_en: Put ね at the end of a sentence to mean "…, isn’t it?" or "…, right?". You say it when you think the listener will agree. It is like the Tamil "-தானே / இல்லையா" in "இன்று திங்கள், இல்லையா?" (Today is Monday, isn’t it?). Or "சீக்கிரம்தானே!" (It’s early, isn’t it!). ね is also used to agree with what someone said: 「そうですね」 ("Yes, that’s right"). Use か (question) when you don’t know the answer. Use ね when you almost know the answer and want to check it.
g04-7.tamil_parallel_en: இன்று திங்கள்தானே? "Today is Monday, isn’t it?" = 今日は 月曜日ですね。 Here ね is roughly the Tamil "-தானே / இல்லையா" (isn’t it).
g04-7.pitfalls_en: When you ask about something for the first time, use か, not ね. If you use ね too much, you sound a bit pushy.

g04-8.explanation_en: All the days of the week end in 〜曜日 (ようび). 月曜日 (திங்கள், Monday; moon). 火曜日 (செவ்வாய், Tuesday; fire). 水曜日 (புதன், Wednesday; water). 木曜日 (வியாழன், Thursday; tree). 金曜日 (வெள்ளி, Friday; metal). 土曜日 (சனி, Saturday; earth). 日曜日 (ஞாயிறு, Sunday; sun). Tamil days are named after things in the sky (திங்கள் = moon, ஞாயிறு = sun, செவ்வாய் = Mars). Japanese days are named after planets too. Even "வெள்ளி" (Friday) = Venus = 金星 is the same! "What day?" = 何曜日 (なんようび). 毎 (まい) = "every". 毎日 = every day (தினமும்). 毎朝 = every morning. 毎晩 = every night. 毎 goes in front of the word, like the Tamil "தின-" (daily). These words don’t take に.
g04-8.tamil_parallel_en: தினமும் காலை ஆறு மணிக்கு எழுந்திருக்கிறேன் "I get up at six every morning" = 毎朝 六時に 起きます。 Here 毎 is roughly the Tamil "தின- / ஒவ்வொரு" (daily / every). Like Tamil day names, the Japanese ones come from the moon, the sun and the planets.
g04-8.formation_en: (月・火・水・木・金・土・日) + 曜日 ; 毎 + 日 / 朝 / 晩
g04-8.pitfalls_en: 火曜日 is かようび (か, not が). 金曜日 is きんようび (not ぎん). ぎん = 銀, as in 銀行 (bank). Don’t add に, as in 毎日に or 毎晩に.

items.L04-q01: 午後 = ごご (பிற்பகல், afternoon / p.m.). Both are short ご. Making it long, as ごうご, is wrong. Changing the sound to ごこ is also wrong.
items.L04-q02: 毎朝 = まいあさ (தினமும் காலை, every morning). 朝 alone is あさ. ちょう is how it is read in other words. It doesn’t fit here.
items.L04-q03: 昨日 = きのう (நேற்று, yesterday). This is a special reading just for this word. Don’t drop the long う sound at the end.
items.L04-q04: よる = 夜 (இரவு, night). 液 has an extra 氵 (water) on the left. 役 is a different character.
items.L04-q05: げつようび = 月曜日 (திங்கள், Monday). 躍 and 耀 look like 曜, but they are different characters. 目 (கண், eye) in place of 日 is also a trap.
items.L04-q06: "What time is it now?" (இப்போது மணி என்ன?) = 今 何時ですか. The answer uses です for now. So きのう (நேற்று, yesterday) doesn’t fit.
items.L04-q07: At eleven at night, you go to bed (寝ます, தூங்குகிறேன்). 起きます (getting up) is something you do in the morning.
items.L04-q08: If today is Saturday, Sunday is "tomorrow" (明日, நாளை). 昨日 (நேற்று, yesterday) would be Friday.
items.L04-q09: Seven hours and thirty minutes = 七時半 (ஏழரை, half past seven). ふん means minutes. It needs a number before it.
items.L04-q10: Nine in the morning = 午前 九時 (a.m., காலை). 午後 or 夜 would mean nine at night. The bank isn’t open then.
items.L04-q11: Monday to Sunday = every day (毎日, தினமும்). 一日 means "a whole day". It doesn’t mean "the whole week".
items.L04-q12: "I didn’t work yesterday" is closest to "I didn’t work all day yesterday" (நேற்று நாள் முழுவதும் வேலை செய்யவில்லை). 明日 and 今日 change the day. 働きました means the opposite.
items.L04-q13: The 24-hour clock is also common in Japan. 午後 五時 = 十七時 (5 p.m. = 17:00). The other choices swap 午前 and 午後, or から and まで.
items.L04-q14: 毎朝 = "every morning" (தினமும் காலை) = 毎日 朝. 今日 起きました means "today only". It happened one time.
items.L04-q15: An exact time with a number → に (Tamil "-க்கு", at). から would mean "I get up from six o’clock". That makes no sense.
items.L04-q16: まで (வரை, until) goes with から (from). に would make it one point in time: "at five o’clock".
items.L04-q17: To join two nouns with "and", use と. の would mean "Saturday’s Sunday". That makes no sense.
items.L04-q18: The sentence has 昨日 (நேற்று, yesterday). So you need the past form 寝ました (தூங்கினேன், I slept). 寝ます is for now or the future. 寝ましたか is a question, and this sentence is not a question.
items.L04-q19: いいえ + past "not" form = 働きませんでした (வேலை செய்யவில்லை, I didn’t work). 働きません is "not" for now. It doesn’t fit "yesterday".
items.L04-q20: 明日 (நாளை, tomorrow) has no number, so it doesn’t take に. You can mark it as the topic with は, or use nothing. 「明日に」 is a common mistake.
items.L04-q21: The reply agrees: 「そうですね」. So the speaker used ね ("isn’t it?", இல்லையா) to check. With か, the reply would start with はい or いいえ.
items.L04-q22: 私は 毎朝 七時に 起きます。 — word with no number (毎朝) → time with number + に → verb. 七時 goes in the ★ slot.
items.L04-q23: 銀行は 九時から 三時までです。 — the start time goes before から. The end time goes before まで. 三時 goes in the ★ slot.
items.L04-q24: 昨日の 晩 何時に 寝ましたか。 — "last night" → "at what time" → verb. 何時に goes in the ★ slot.
items.L04-q25: ［1］ から goes with まで (from Monday, திங்கள் முதல்). ［2］ It is about last night, so use the past form 寝ました (தூங்கினேன், I slept). ［3］ You get up and go to work in the morning. So seven in the morning = 午前 七時.
